content.text: The redline validates. Submitting the finding.

input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled)
input.rationale: Section 6.1 is a field-of-use/non-compete covenant binding the Company (our party), so it is in scope; the parallel restriction on HDI in Section 6.3 (two years post-term) benefits us and is not flagged. Measured against the fallback, 6.1 fails on two material terms. (1) Scope is not limited to a named competing product: it reaches "products substantially similar to Deerskin Products" and, by the "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled" formulation, an open-ended class of third-party products. (2) There is no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions — the only carve-out is Section 6.2 (closeout merchandise) plus the Section 1.1 exclusions for closeouts and the Joan Cook Catalog — so an acquisition of, or internal build of, a leather apparel web business would breach. The 12-month cap is also not met in substance: although the covenant is term-only (no post-term tail, which keeps this out of walk-away territory), Section 4.1 makes the one-year term automatically renewing on each anniversary, so the restriction can run indefinitely. Preferred is deletion, but HDI is building and hosting a self-contained Deerskin site, takes the exclusive "Deerskin" brand right and accepts a longer reciprocal covenant in 6.3, so the existing bargain makes outright deletion disproportionate; we therefore propose the narrowed fallback — Deerskin Products only, capped at twelve months, with an internal-development and acquisition carve-out.

proposal.summary: Narrow Section 6.1 Company non-compete to Deerskin Products only, cap at 12 months, and add internal-development/acquisition carve-out
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build, so our position is that the Section 6.1 covenant on the Company should come out. As a fallback we have narrowed it to Deerskin Products only (deleting the open-ended "substantially similar" products and "companies similar to" language), capped it at twelve months, and carved out internal development and acquisitions; HDI's exclusive "Deerskin" brand right and its Section 6.3 protection are unaffected.

ops.newText: during the term of this Agreement (but in no event for more than twelve (12) months following the Effective Date), the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products

ops.text: Nothing in Section 6.1 shall restrict the Company from (i) developing, offering or selling any products other than Deerskin Products through any channel, (ii) internally developing any product, catalog or web site, or (iii) acquiring, being acquired by, or continuing to operate the business of, any person or entity engaged in the offering of apparel or accessories on the Internet.
